correctness.rationale: The exact BFGS-conjugation identity yields the product of squared cosine overlaps. The Poisson-kernel direction law and ergodic logarithmic integral yield Q(r); the positive finite-rank transfer operator with even Perron eigenfunction yields Lambda(r). Fourier products give the displayed 3-by-3 T and exact cubic, and nonzero starting forms have nonzero Perron coefficient. Direct BFGS code identities, 100 rational characteristic polynomials, quadrature, and sample-path rates passed. Limits are proved analytically, not inferred from simulations.

originality.rationale: The closest matching 2016 original establishes identical inverse-BFGS dynamics but only a general squared-error upper bound. In the exact isotropic model that bound is 1/2 while the present theorem establishes the strict 3/8 mean-square rate and 1/16 almost-sure rate. The 2020 original RBFGS optimization analysis and the 2018 accelerated matrix-inversion work do not state the two sharp planar Gaussian rates. Matching implications and transfer-operator aliases were searched. Priority remains subject to independent literature examination, especially unindexed special-case products.

value.rationale: The exact fixed-Hessian planar Gaussian rate is a motivated analytic benchmark for the randomized inverse-BFGS algorithm. It replaces a nonsharp general 1/2 isotropic bound with the exact 3/8 factor and reveals a substantially faster 1/16 typical factor; the anisotropic cubic characterizes all positive condition ratios with monotone slowdown. This is an exact, natural parameter-dependent numerical invariant, not an arbitrary finite sample or routine substitution. No claim for moving Hessians, higher dimensions or downstream optimization iterates.
